def: The threshold, budget or top-k selection that turns a model's scores into actions.
A problem in which past decisions determine which outcomes are observed, so only some cases ever receive a label.
A model that estimates how much an action changes an individual's outcome, rather than how likely the outcome is.
A randomised experiment that assigns units to the current system or a new one and compares a pre-chosen outcome.
A metric that must not get worse in an experiment, such as latency or complaints, whatever the primary metric does.
Checking an experiment repeatedly and stopping at the first significant result, which inflates the false-positive rate.
A split of units between experiment arms that differs from the intended ratio by more than chance allows, signalling a bug in assignment or logging.
Running a model on live traffic without acting on its outputs, to compare them with what actually happens.
Exposing a new model or version to a small share of traffic while watching guardrail metrics.
Any change between training and deployment in the distribution of inputs, labels or their relationship.
A change in the distribution of the inputs while the relationship between inputs and outcome stays the same.
A change over time in the relationship between the inputs and the outcome.
A drift measure summing (current share minus reference share) times the log of their ratio across bins of the reference distribution.
A release pattern in which a candidate model must beat the current production model on a backtest and live traffic before replacing it.
